$comment: THE ONE FILE YOU EDIT. Everything about who you run ads for, and where their
numbers come from, lives here. Nothing about your business is hardcoded in the
app. Run `npm run doctor` after any change — it checks this file against your
environment and tells you exactly what is still missing.
Secrets NEVER go in here. This file is committed to git. Tokens go in .env.local
(locally) or your host's environment variables (in production).
One entry per person you run ads for. `key` is the short internal id used
everywhere — lowercase, no spaces, and never changed once data exists.
`timezone` is the ad account's REPORTING timezone in Meta, not where the
person lives. Get it wrong and days land in the wrong bucket.
`currency` is the currency Meta BILLS this ad account in. It applies to ad
spend and budgets only. Sales money is always USD (see docs/DATA-RULES.md).
`salesCalendarIds` are the GoHighLevel calendar ids that count as a SALES
call. Onboarding calls, coaching calls, and reschedule calendars must NOT
be listed. Run `npm run calendars` to list the real ids in your data.
`matchTokens` are lowercase fragments that identify this creator wherever
their name appears in incoming data. Keep them specific enough that two
creators can never both match the same text.
creators.name: Example Creator

$comment: Where the sales tracker lives. Set `enabled` to false and Ads V2 still runs —
you get spend, DMs and booked calls, but no revenue and therefore no ROAS.
`tabs`: "monthly" reads one tab per month named by `monthTabFormat`;
"single" reads one fixed tab named by `tab`.
`columns` maps YOUR sheet's column letters onto the fields Ads V2 needs.
Only `date` and `prospectName` are required. Every other field left empty
simply produces no data for that field rather than a wrong guess.
`manychatLink` is the highest-value optional column by a wide margin: it is
what ties a closed sale back to the DM, and therefore to the ad. Without it
sales attribute by name matching, which is much weaker.
`keywordFromAdName` is how a spend row learns its keyword, and it is the
whole join between money spent and DMs received.
THE NAMING RULE: the keyword is the LAST WORD of the ad name. The name is
split on | : ( ) [ ] { } _ - and the last word of the last piece wins:
"TEST | Direct CTA | TRIM"   -> trim
"Q3 Scaling (PRIMED)"        -> primed
"Lead Magnet | 50 | Tempo"   -> tempo
Name an ad without its keyword at the end and its spend still records, but
it can never be credited to a DM, a call, or a sale.
`factsLookbackDays` is how far back every sync rebuilds. It must comfortably
exceed your longest display window (30 days) plus your sales cycle.
